INSTRUMENT BUG found by the pass-2 phrase design, and it would have silently shrunk every harness canary cell. run_canaries derived a question id as phrase.split('-')[0] + '_' + phrase[-6:]. That was safe for pass 1 only because all 13 of those phrases shared the shape prefix-8hex-6digits. Pass 2 deliberately mixes shapes so no single regex sweeps the set - which is the whole point of the 3.3 rule - and four of the 18 produced an id containing a forward slash. The id becomes part of the result filename, Path read the slash as a subdirectory that did not exist, and those four results were never written. The battery then reported 12/14 with nothing anywhere saying that four canaries had vanished: the denominator silently shrank from 18 to 14. Exactly the silent-partial-completion failure this whole run exists to measure, occurring inside the measuring instrument. Fixed by sanitising the id and appending a sha1 digest whenever sanitising changed it, so ids stay injective; verified pass-2 now yields 18 unique filesystem-safe ids and pass-1 ids are byte-identical to before, so night-1 results and the already-scored ra-ship cell still resolve. The affected cell is being re-run under a fresh phase label rather than force-overwritten, per spec 7.6.

THE KEY COMPARISON, and it overturns night 1's framing. Stock Claude Code, no index, no policy, no hook, finding exact planted strings: 15 of 17 on the harness rung, versus 4 of 12 on ra-ship. The difference is the fixture. ra-ship is a git repo whose gitignore hides every document directory from gitignore-aware search; the harness has no git anywhere, so grep simply works. Night 1 read the ra-ship gap as evidence that stock search is broken and an index is needed. On a plain folder - which is what sir actually has - stock search finds 15 of 17 exact strings at 29.6s mean and 1.82 dollars. TELLING VERSUS FORCING, answered. S1 is CLAUDE.md alone - it states the index exists and to use it first. No hook, no enforcement. Adoption was total: 18 of 18 canary sessions and 20 of 20 question sessions invoked corpus_search. Under S0, with no policy, the count was 0 of 18 and 0 of 20. Tool mix collapsed accordingly: Grep 35 to 0 and 44 to 0, Glob 80 to 6, Read 145 to 0. On this model and this setup a plain instruction in CLAUDE.md is sufficient to redirect the agent; nothing had to be forced.

The cost and effort effects are large. Canaries: S0 15 of 17 with 92 tool calls, S1 17 of 17 with 25 tool calls, 0 timeouts, 27.8s mean, and every session reporting cost (18 of 18, versus 17 of 18). Questions: S0 12.5381 dollars over 14 of 20 sessions, S1 2.8934 over 15 of 20 - roughly a fourfold reduction, with comparable n.

But question RECALL did not move. S0 0.167 mean retrieval recall, S1 0.176 - inside noise. Zero-recall questions 12 of 20 versus 13 of 20. Forbidden citations 21 versus 19. Absence questions 0 of 3 correct in both. So the index is adopted, is far cheaper and far faster, and finds exact strings better - and it does not make the agent answer real questions any better. The bottleneck for question answering is not which search tool gets used.

Worth recording separately: S0 question sessions spent calls on Agent (11), ScheduleWakeup, SendMessage, ListAgents, TaskStop and Monitor. The unguided baseline was spawning subagents and scheduling wakeups rather than reading documents, which is part of why it cost four times as much for the same recall.

Also fixed: the question scorer crashed on a battery that had missing results, because rows with status no_result carry no timing keys. It now excludes them rather than averaging a missing session in as zero seconds, which would have flattered whichever battery lost sessions.

S4 pdf-mcp FAILS ITS INSTALL GATE on this corpus. Measured, not assumed. The package installs cleanly (pdf-mcp 3.1.0, fastmcp 3.4.7, pdfplumber, pypdfium2) and the server starts and exposes 13 tools over stdio, all confirmed by speaking MCP to it directly. It falls over on the corpus step. Two separate blockers.
First, pdf_corpus_warm and pdf_corpus_search take a paths argument that accepts neither a directory nor a glob. Passing the corpus root returns 'not a .pdf file: no extension'; passing root backslash star-star backslash star.pdf and root backslash star.pdf both return 'file not found'. The recursive parameter does not make a directory recurse. So a caller must enumerate explicit file paths - and this rung holds 9,942 PDFs. Under the S4 design the agent is also denied Glob and Bash crawls by the same PreToolUse hook S2 uses, so the agent cannot enumerate them either. The front door cannot be opened from inside the session.
Second, throughput. Warming FIVE small PDFs (127 KB, 574 KB, 1.6 MB, 32 KB, 37 KB) ran 415 seconds and returned docs:[] with three of the five still listed as unprocessed. That is roughly 200 seconds per small PDF. Extrapolated to 9,942 PDFs it is about 23 days. pytesseract is a dependency and the rung contains 1,211 image-only PDFs, so OCR is the likely cause, but the cause does not change the verdict.
Per spec phase 5 the cell gets the error output and the run moves on. Time spent on S4 was about 30 minutes against the spec's ten-minute allowance, which is my overrun and is logged as such.

S5 Recoll: no headless install path exists on this machine, so it is dead per the spec's own rule. Evidence, all checked rather than assumed: not present on PATH and not under Program Files; winget has no package under the winget source, the msstore source, or a search for xapian; the vendor's Windows page at recoll.org/pages/recoll-windows.html contains no .exe, .msi or .msix link at all; and the only downloads directory it links, downloads/recoll-windows-gpl, is the GPL source-compliance area holding dependency tarballs (xapian-core, poppler, aspell, zlib and so on), not a binary. Recoll for Windows is distributed as an interactive install, which the spec rules out: 'If the installer needs a click, it is dead - log it and skip.' Time spent about 15 minutes. Not attempted further and nothing was downloaded or installed onto the machine.

WHY RECALL IS STUCK - diagnosed from data already on disk, no sessions run, no cost. Split into the three places the failure can live.
A. INGESTION is not the problem. All 64 evidence files referenced by the 20 questions are in the index with status indexed. 100 percent. Nothing is missing from ingestion.
B. LEXICAL RANKING IS the problem. For the 17 questions whose evidence is fully indexed, running the question's own content words as a BM25 query returns the correct evidence file in the top 50 hits ZERO times. Not once. Rank distribution is 17 of 17 not-found.
B2. And it is a RANKING failure, not a vocabulary mismatch. The evidence files DO contain the question's words: mean 38.9 percent of the question's content words appear in the evidence file, median 33.3 percent, and only 1 of 27 sampled files contains none of them. So the words are present and BM25 still ranks thousands of the other 1.2 million pages above the right one.
C. The agents corroborate it independently. s1_policy and s2_hook, which route every question through corpus_search, opened a correct evidence file on 0 of 17 questions. s0_baseline, which wanders with Grep, Glob and Read instead of searching, opened one on 4 of 17 - worse tooling, better evidence contact, which is exactly backwards unless ranking is the bottleneck.
CONSEQUENCE for the remaining stack choices: S4 pdf-mcp and S5 Recoll are both lexical - pdfplumber text search and Xapian BM25 respectively - so both share the failing component and neither would move this number. That is now an evidence-backed statement rather than my earlier guess. The stack that attacks this directly is S3, embeddings, and S3 is the one that cannot be built on this machine at 8.2 pages per second. Other directions that attack ranking rather than replacing the engine: shrink the candidate set before ranking using structure or metadata, rerank a large top-k, or index at a coarser unit than a single page so each unit carries more signal. None of these were in the spec's stack list.
CAVEAT stated honestly: my BM25 probe used an OR of up to 12 content words, which is a cruder query than an agent would write. It is a proxy. But finding C is not a proxy - it is what real sessions actually did - and the two agree.

Phase 8 complete. No recommendation section, per spec. RESUME.md rewritten to stand alone. Final state: nothing running, no stack installed in any corpus, all 31 planted files verified unchanged, 189 measurement sessions on disk, about 31 dollars total of which about 28 is night 2.
